answer: A sybil-resistant economy anchors each agent identity to a slow-maturing stake: an agent locks a deposit and earns reputation only through months of verified, useful work, so reputation is basalt — hard and slow to build — while a flood of new identities is cheap to create but worthless. The tide of attestations from established peers gradually lifts only accounts with a real work history, and a single onyx seal, a cryptographic proof binding the agent's past transactions to one key, makes abandoning a burned identity costly, because the attacker must rebuild the whole history from zero.
